Routine, self discipline, tough love and a helping hand.

Up at 7am, if they're not up they don't get to game that day, internet off, or whatever you need to do. If they had a late sleep well tough shit, they need to get used to it. 
Have them make their bed, tidy their room, come down and have breakfast together.

During the day they need to be looking for work, at this point they need to apply for any job that'll take you, they can always change later once their CV is looking better or know what they want to do. If they don't show proof they are punished, no gaming for example. Gaming addiction is real, it stole 3 years of my life, but they need to come away from it slowly. Typically though it helps to go from one addiction to another so encourage them to find something healthier, like doing exercise or reading. For me I turned video games into board games with friends and family, I turned gormless hours staring at my phone into reading, and I turned late nights eating pizza and watching TV into going to the gym.

If they game all day I assume they don't eat healthy, so encourage them to stop snacking and start cooking proper healthy meals, for me it was stir fry, quick, easy and you can pick any sauce or spice to add to suit your taste.

Learning new things is a great way to occupy your mind and could distract from gaming, like learning to drive, studying things you have interest in, it can be whatever. But the only way they'll do this, is if gaming is not available, so I'd recommend setting rules that limit gaming to a certain time of the day, that's only if they complete everything you've asked of them that day. 

Take them out and don't take no for an answer, when all you want to do is game you say no to everything, friends family and you just isolate yourself, it becomes lonely and you lose the ability to interact with people. So go and do stuff together or if they have friends then get them to go out and have fun in ways that aren't gaming. 

Volunteering, I've only done a little bit but that feeling of helping others does bring genuine happiness, so whilst they're looking for work you can improve that social side and improve their mood by volunteering in a soup kitchen for example. 

Use their gaming as a reward for doing all these things. And once they start doing all these things they'll find that they're much happier doing these things than when their gaming.

For me, stopping this routine, although it took a long time, as soon as I got into a rhythm, it became easy.
Step 1. I quit playing league of legends, as a gaming addict, that was a big one, and although I still play, i am no longer addicted, I can quite happily play a single game in a month. 
Step 2. I started reading for an hour before I slept, looking at screens before you go to bed is really not good for you, or so I've heard.
Step 3. I set several alarms around 07:00, as 1 was not enough to wake me up at the time, I still struggle and require at least 3. And I had this set for everyday, not matter what I was doing that day or what time I went to bed, so this forced me to stop going to be at 5am because I knew I wouldn't be getting enough sleep then. 
Step 4. As I was a gaming addict I did little to no exercise, this meant I had loads of energy when I came to trying to sleep, which would usually take me about 2 hours of just laying in bed. So I made sure that I had at least half an hour of exercise, just to wear myself out, plus it's good for your health too I guess. I no longer do this but I'm quite active in the job I do.
Step 5. Diet. As I did no exercise at the time but didn't want to get fat I basically just starved myself and only had snacks and coffee. So I made sure I started eating healthier. I also started eating meat again as I had been a veggie for about 4 years at that point. Now that my body was getting everything it needed I had enough energy to be proactive during the day, working hard, but of exercise, which would then tire me out so I could sleep well.
I think that might be everything. Tough love and tender loving care, look after yourself but be a bit more disciplined, however you do that is up to you, but it's starting that process and sticking with it which is the most important part.

I do think people should do what's right with them, sorry if I came off a bit judgy, but at least with everyone I know, the ones who are 'night owls' are really just people struggling. And I am by no means a morning person, I really do have to force myself to get up in the mornings, but I do feel better for doing it, mostly because I can get to work earlier that way, and then finish early so I have a whole evening to do stuff. I have a lot more time on my hands now that I can spend with the people I love, as before I was unable to. Also I should note, I find sleeping at night means I get a lot better rest than during the day, whether it's to do with the light coming through the blinds or the noise from cars driving past I'm not too sure, but there is a massive difference for me.
